55.0.0.en: 1 “Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. 2 Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness. 3 Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David. 4 Behold, I have given him for a witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people. 5 Behold, thou shalt call a nation that thou knowest not, and nations that knew not thee shall run unto thee because of the LORD thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he hath glorified thee.”

55.0.1.en: The divine call to enjoy the free salvation of the Lord carries the following items:

55.0.2.en: a. A general call to the thirsty: “Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price” [1]. It is a general call to all; the doors of the Church are open before everyone, and whoever feels need, that is, “the thirsty,” listens to it. As the Lord said: “Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled” (Mt 5:6).

55.0.3.en: As we have repeated before, water in the Holy Bible sometimes signifies the Holy Spirit who works in the waters of Baptism; as though the call here is addressed to all to enjoy Baptism freely.

55.0.4.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus speaks of the gift of Baptism, saying: [Do not hesitate however long the journey may be, whether by sea or by land, so long as the gift is offered to you, however many or few the obstacles, for Isaiah calls you: “Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye...” How swift are the mercies of God, how easy is the covenant! You receive this blessing as soon as you desire it. He accepts your very desire as a great price. He thirsts for your thirst, and satisfies all who desire the mystery. He offers kindness to all who ask kindness. He is ready to give generously, and rejoices in giving more than those who receive rejoice.]

55.0.5.en: b. A satisfying giving to all. This free gift, which is not bought with silver or with a price, offers every person his needs; so the mature find wine that gladdens them and the little ones find milk that sustains them.

55.1.0.en: The spiritual wine enjoyed by the mature signifies the state of joy enjoyed by those who have reached spiritual stature, so that their souls delight in the fatness of the Lord [2]. As the Spiritual Elder says: [Blessed is he who carries Your remembrance in his heart at all times, for his soul is always made drunk with Your sweetness.]

55.1.1.en: The spiritual milk offered to the little ones signifies God’s gentleness toward beginners, giving them what suits their spiritual stomach until they grow and mature; He knows how to offer each one what is for his edification, peace, satisfaction and refreshment.

55.1.2.en: Thus no one feels deprived, but as it is said: “eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness” [2].

55.1.3.en: * Do you not want to be satisfied? And how can that be?

55.1.4.en: The body longs to be satisfied, but hunger returns to it again after digestion; therefore the Lord Christ says: “Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again” (Lk 4:13)...

55.1.5.en: Then let us hunger and thirst after righteousness, that we may be satisfied from it..

55.1.6.en: May our inner man hunger and thirst, that he may have the food and drink suited to him.

55.1.7.en: He (the Lord) has said: “I am the bread which came down from heaven” (Jn 6:41). This is the bread of the hungry.

55.1.8.en: Let us also long to drink like the thirsty, “For with thee is the fountain of life” (Ps 36:9).

55.1.9.en: * Blessed is he who has forgotten the talk of the world through his talk with You, for from You all his needs are fulfilled.

55.1.10.en: You are his food and his drink...!

55.1.11.en: You gave the Spirit of Your Son in his heart, and the Spirit gave him boldness to ask of You all that is Yours, as a son asks of his father! His talk is with You at all times, for he knows no father but You!.

55.1.12.en: The Spiritual Elder * Ah! I shall not be satisfied until Your glory is revealed before me...!

55.1.13.en: He who possesses You has all his desires satisfied!

55.1.14.en: But how hideous is my wretchedness! Woe is me, O my God, for my heart tends to flee from You; to flee from You, the true Rich One and true joy, in order to follow the world in which there is nothing but sorrow and pain.

55.1.15.en: St. Augustine * Let them be all the more in need that they may deserve to be satisfied, lest while they show an arrogant fullness they be deprived of the bread that gives healthy life.

55.1.16.en: “Seek ye the LORD,” O needy, hungry and thirsty, for He is the living bread which came down from heaven (Jn 6:33, 51).

55.1.17.en: “Seek ye the LORD, and ye shall live.” You seek bread that your body may live, and the Lord seeks you that your souls may live.

55.1.18.en: St. Augustine * [“His eyes shall be red with wine, and his teeth white with milk” (Gen 49:12)].

55.1.19.en: His eyes are red with wine; these are His spiritual people who are made drunk with His cup; and His teeth are whiter than milk, which is the words with which are nursed the babes who are not yet fit for strong meat, as the Apostle says (1 Cor 3:2; 1 Pet 2:2).

55.1.20.en: St. Augustine * Be drunk, but be careful of the source. If you drink abundantly from the wonderful cup of the Lord, your drunkenness will be seen in your works, and will appear in your holy love of righteousness, and finally in the estrangement of your mind from earthly things to heavenly things.

55.1.21.en: St. Augustine Let us then draw near to our Christ and buy His wine and milk freely, according to His promise and His call.

55.2.0.en: c. Entering into an everlasting covenant to establish the fallen kingdom of David according to the sure divine promise: “and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David” [3]. Through this covenant we become kings (Rev 5:10) belonging to the King of kings, of whom it is said: “Behold, I have given him for a witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people” [4]. He is the King who lays down the law of the New Testament and the new commandment, not for a particular people but for all peoples.

55.3.0.en: d. The acceptance of the pagan Gentiles who return to God by faith: “Behold, thou shalt call a nation that thou knowest not, and nations that knew not thee shall run unto thee because of the LORD thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he hath glorified thee” [5].

55.3.1.en: This matter was not acceptable to the ancient people, and even after the door was opened before the Gentiles, the Church throughout the world remained for centuries in amazement before God’s love for all mankind, as He draws them from paganism and its abominations to proclaim the glory of God. In wonder St. Augustine says: [How have the Gentiles entered into the faith so swiftly...?! We ask them: What do you want? They answer: “To know the glory of God.”]

55.4.0.en: 6 “Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: 7 Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon. 8 For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. 9 For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts. 10 For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: 11 So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it. 12 For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands. 13 Instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree: and it shall be to the LORD for a name, for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off.”

55.4.1.en: Before this general, free and holy call to the thirsty, it is fitting for man to declare his response to it and his acceptance of it in practice by the following means:

55.4.2.en: a. Prayer, or seeking God in order to meet Him: “Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near” [6].

55.4.3.en: If God loved us first, and came down to us to declare that He is not far from us but at the doors of our hearts, knocking that we may open to Him and He may enter (Rev 3:20), then it is fitting for us to seek Him, asking Him to take the keys of our hearts, that He may open and enter and shut, so that no one else shares with Him in our hearts, since He “openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth.”

55.4.4.en: The declaration of our acceptance of God’s love through prayer is a response of love to love, and the soul’s declaration of her desire for her unique Bridegroom, who asks for her hand forever.

55.5.0.en: b. Repentance: “Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon” [7].

55.5.1.en: What does repentance mean but the declaration of accepting light rather than darkness, and Christ rather than Belial (2 Cor 6:14)?!

55.5.2.en: Repentance is the way that St. John the Baptist prepared for the Lord Christ, and which the disciples preached to prepare mankind to receive His Kingdom within them!

55.6.0.en: c. Relying on God’s wisdom and trusting in His plan and His dispensations toward us, for He says: “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts” [8-9].

55.6.1.en: Our faith in the heavenly Bridegroom requires relying on Him with confidence in His abilities as the Almighty, all-wise and all-loving, who knows how to plan for His bride, for her edification and salvation, even if His plan appears harsh and His dispensations bitter.

55.7.0.en: d. Being watered by the word of the Lord that gives fruit: “For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: so shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it” [10-11].

55.7.1.en: The Word of God came down incarnate to water human nature with His blood as a unique rain able to re-create it and renew it, turning it from a barren wilderness inhabited by fierce beasts into a fruitful paradise inhabited by the Holy Trinity, in which the heavenly and also the earthly rejoice. So it is fitting for us also to receive the written word of God, not for purely intellectual study, but as a life lived out that bears divine fruit.

55.8.0.en: e. Constant praise is a sign of accepting the Bridegroom in the heart and responding to Him inwardly: “For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands” [12].

55.8.1.en: Going out with joy means the soul’s going out from the “ego,” and her widening in love on behalf of her Bridegroom and all His beloved, her widening to the heavenly and the earthly... She goes out in order to return with all in peace and reconciliation with God, the angels and men. This wide love creates an atmosphere of joy through which the mountains and the hills sing, that is, the company of believers around you, as they see an eternal wedding taking place within you. As for the trees of the field clapping their hands, it means that joy is not in the tongue only but is declared by deed (by the hands)...

55.8.2.en: f. Abundant positive fruit. It is not enough to pull up the thorn and the brier, but the fir tree and the myrtle tree must appear as a sign of our being sealed with the name of the Lord, the Giver of spiritual fruit. In other words, our acceptance of His call does not mean only our leaving evil, but our doing the righteousness of Christ and practicing His holy, fruitful life by the work of His Holy Spirit in us.

56.0.s.en: 1. A house of prayer for all peoples:

56.0.0.en: 1 Thus saith the LORD, “Keep ye judgment, and do justice: for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed. 2 Blessed is the man that doeth this, and the son of man that layeth hold on it; that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and keepeth his hand from doing any evil.” 3 Neither let the son of the stranger, that hath joined himself to the LORD, speak, saying, “The LORD hath utterly separated me from his people”: neither let the eunuch say, “Behold, I am a dry tree.” 4 For thus saith the LORD unto the eunuchs that keep my sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and take hold of my covenant; 5 “Even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off. 6 Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the LORD, to serve him, and to love the name of the LORD, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant; 7 Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.” 8 The Lord GOD which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, “Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him.”

56.0.1.en: In the previous chapter the call was to all the thirsty (Isa 55:1); to Jews and Gentiles, to the thirsty and the hungry, to the blind and the deaf, and so on... that they might drink from the springs of the Gospel of free salvation and the gift of the Spirit offered to the Church of the New Testament. Now, fearing that someone might draw back from the gift, counting himself a stranger, the son of a stranger because he was born of a pagan family that denied the faith, or because he is barren by nature as a eunuch or a dry tree, he began to encourage all to enter through the doors of God’s wide mercies:

56.0.2.en: a. The salvation of the Lord is not far off, “for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed” [1]. As to time, there remained only seven centuries until the coming of the Lord Christ, the Savior of the world, that is, about 700 years, and a thousand years in the sight of the Lord are as one day (Ps 90:4). But what is more important is that the salvation of the Lord is near to everyone, because the Word is inside the heart, and the Cross of the Lord can be revealed in every soul. As St. Augustine said: [In my folly I was seeking You outside... and You were within me, deeper than my depths and higher than my heights.]

56.0.3.en: The way of our salvation is in our depths, because He has given us the Holy Spirit of God and our membership in one body, the Lord Christ, through Baptism... so we have become a dwelling for God and a temple for Him; therefore the Apostle says: “The word is nigh thee, even in thy mouth, and in thy heart” (Rom 10:8).

56.0.4.en: When St. Ephrem the Syrian speaks of the birth of the Lord of glory Jesus, he directs our eyes inward, where the Lord drew near to us and came to dwell by faith in our hearts (Eph 3:17).

56.0.5.en: * Let every man adorn the doors of his heart on this feast, for the Holy Spirit longs to enter and dwell in the heart and sanctify it. He goes about to all the doors to see where He may enter!

56.0.6.en: Let the doors of the heart rejoice on this feast together with the doors of the churches, so that the holy God may rejoice in the holy temple, the mouths of children may exult in praise, and Christ may rejoice on His feast as a mighty one.

56.0.7.en: St. Ephrem the Syrian b. By saying “Keep ye judgment, and do justice: for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed” [1] he reveals the concept of virtue. For we are bound to keep judgment and to practice justice, that is, to walk according to the divine commandment, which is judgment and justice, and this is difficult, indeed impossible, for human nature in itself. But if salvation is declared in the heart and the righteousness of Christ is manifested, the commandment becomes easy and possible, indeed natural and sweet, because the One who fulfills it is God who dwells in us and works by His Spirit in us.

56.0.8.en: Virtue according to St. John Cassian is [that through which we offer the kingdom of the heart to Christ].

56.0.9.en: We deliver the heart to Him that He may work in it and transform us into His likeness and image. Origen says: [We were created in the image of Christ, therefore virtues in his view are that we become one with Him, for He Himself is the virtues that we acquire]. [He is justice, wisdom and truth at the same time. Therefore whoever truly practices these virtues is a true partaker of the divine nature].

56.0.10.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus says: [God is called love and peace; by these names He urges us to be formed according to these virtues, which are His marks].

56.0.11.en: Virtue is the work of God in His believers who accept His call and respond to His love:

56.0.12.en: * Do we not notice that there is nothing we do without Christ.

56.0.13.en: * We cannot run in the way of God except when carried on the wings of the Spirit.

56.0.14.en: * There is none stronger than he who enjoys heavenly help, as there is none weaker than he who is deprived of it.

56.0.15.en: St. John Chrysostom * God is holy and sanctifies, God is righteous and justifies.

56.1.0.en: St. Augustine c. This divine gift is free, but it is not given by compulsion nor to the slack, but to those who respond to it in practice. “Blessed is the man that doeth this, and the son of man that layeth hold on it; that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and keepeth his hand from doing any evil” [2]. For if God has given us His resurrection, or His risen life, as a “sabbath,” that is, rest for our souls, then it is fitting for us to live this life and keep it, and not to live in the misery and corruption of death. Let us keep our hand from the practice of every evil work, lest we be subject to the death of sin, but remain in the Lord, our true “sabbath.”

56.1.1.en: Our true sabbath is our Lord Jesus, the Sacrifice risen from the dead; in Him the Father finds His rest (His sabbath) concerning us, as we are justified in Him and counted His children; and in Him we find our rest, as we find in Him a place in the bosom of the Father.

56.1.2.en: * We ourselves become the seventh day (the sabbath) when we are filled with the blessings of God and His sanctification and are overflowing with them.

56.2.0.en: St. Augustine d. The turning of strangers into sons of the house of God: “Neither let the son of the stranger, that hath joined himself to the LORD, speak, saying, The LORD hath utterly separated me from his people” [3]. Rather they enjoy the divine covenant, and have the right to worship and to serve the house of the Lord. “Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the LORD, to serve him, and to love the name of the LORD, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant” [6].

56.2.1.en: What does the acceptance of strangers as sons of the house of the Lord and their taking hold of the divine covenant mean? It is the enjoyment of union with the Lord Christ, to enter the heavenly sanctuaries without hindrance, as holy sons in Him and as members of His body, having the right to union with the Father by the Holy Spirit through the blood of the covenant, the atoning blood of the Lord Christ.

56.2.2.en: The opening of the door of salvation before strangers that they may become sons of God, with the right to worship as well as to serve, gives hope to all, and as St. Hippolytus says:

56.2.3.en: [The “Word” shows His tenderness while showing no partiality...

56.2.4.en: He loves to teach the ignorant, and to bring the erring back to the true way.

56.2.5.en: Those who live in faith find Him easily, those who have the pure eye and the holy heart, who desire to knock at the door; for He opens the door quickly.

56.2.6.en: He drives away none of His servants as unworthy of the divine mysteries.

56.2.7.en: He does not honor the rich more than the poor, nor does He despise the poor because of his poverty.

56.2.8.en: He does not scorn the barbarian nor reject the eunuch as one who is not a man [3-4].

56.2.9.en: He does not hate females because of the disobedience of the woman at the beginning (Eve), nor reject males because of the disobedience of the man.

56.2.10.en: He seeks all, and desires the salvation of all, longing to make all sons of God, calling all the saints as one perfect man.]

56.2.11.en: e. He gives the eunuchs sons: “Neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree” [3]. Physical eunuchs were not permitted to be admitted to the priesthood (Lev 21:20) nor to join the people in the assemblies... (Deut 23:1).

56.2.12.en: Now that the doors of God’s mercies have been opened, there is no spiritual eunuch in the Church of God, for there is none barren among them, but all bear twins (Song 4:2)... All bear witness to God and bring forth sons for Him. It is as though our meeting with the Lord does not stop at our right to enter His house and enjoy His covenant, but gives us the power to witness to Him and to bear fruit.

56.2.13.en: God promised His people, if they obeyed, “Thou shalt be blessed above all people: there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle” (Deut 7:14).

56.3.0.en: f. He raises the believers up as heroes, and their memory remains immortal forever, even in heaven. “Even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off” [5]. How wonderful! The Lord came to us incarnate that He might die on our earth and rise to lift us up to His heavenly house, immortal, death unable to shatter us, but our names will be engraved in the book of God and on the palm of His hand forever.

56.3.1.en: The secret of the immortality of our name in the heavenly divine house is our union with the Lord Christ, as we are the living stones resting on the cornerstone. “Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ. Wherefore also it is contained in the scripture, Behold, I lay in Sion a chief corner stone, elect, precious: and he that believeth on him shall not be confounded” (1 Pet 2:5-6).

56.4.0.en: g. Enjoying a worship that is joyful to us and a source of the Father’s pleasure: “Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people” [7].

56.4.1.en: What does this mean but our enjoying worship not as a duty we are bound to or as formalities, but as a joyful ascent on the holy mountain of the Lord and rejoicing in the heavenly house of the Lord, as a house of prayer in which we offer our life as a burnt offering of love and a holy sacrifice united with the sacrifice of the holy Christ; we exult, and the Father accepts it as bearing the sweet fragrance of Christ, the source of His pleasure. Tertullian says: [This sacrifice comes out of every heart, is nourished on faith, and observes the truth. It enters in innocence and purity, in chastity, and is adorned with love. We must guard it with the greatness of good works, offering psalms and hymns on the altar of God that we may receive all things from Him].

56.4.2.en: h. The opening of the house of the Lord before all peoples, among them the outcasts of Israel. Perhaps the outcasts here are meant to include the return of Christians who have fallen (the new Israel), for the doors of the house of the Lord are open to all, even to the believers who have fallen or gone astray, since some heretics refused to accept them. St. Cyprian wrote two wonderful (works) on this matter under the title Repentance.

56.4.3.en: Thus this chapter presents to us a living picture of the Church of the New Testament, whose marks are these: she is a house of prayer, that is, the place of God’s meeting with men, where we enjoy a living fellowship with God who is near us, who makes His dwelling in us [1]. She is the dwelling of truth and justice, since we are united with our Christ, the Righteous One, who is able to justify the ungodly, offering them Himself as truth, justice, righteousness and love [1]. The mark of this house is the sanctification of free will: its doors are open to all without exception, but without compulsion or constraint [2-3]; whoever enters it has estrangement from God removed from him and becomes one of the household of God, but whoever wishes to remain outside, there is none who compels him to enter. Inside this house all become like fruitful trees that know no dryness [3], because it is the house of the Lord and His fruitful paradise. Whoever dwells in it lives with his Savior in His glories forever, so his name is engraved in heaven and a memorial that is never shattered is set up for him [5]. Inside is unceasing eternal joy and holy, heavenly, angelic worship (Isa 57:7). Finally, it is the house of mercy: whoever leaves it, the doors are not shut in his face, but the arms of the Lord remain waiting for his return.

56.5.s.en: 2. The rejection of those who deny the faith:

56.5.0.en: 9 “All ye beasts of the field, come to devour, yea, all ye beasts in the forest. 10 His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark; sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber. 11 Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter. 12 Come ye, say they, I will fetch wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink; and to morrow shall be as this day, and much more abundant.”

56.5.1.en: Though the house of the Lord is open to all, even to fallen believers, whatever their fall, entering it is through “repentance.”

56.5.2.en: Whoever remains in his denial remains outside the house of the Lord, under no shepherding, inevitably exposed to the beasts of prey in the outer wilderness that he has chosen.

56.6.0.en: The prophet looks at those who reject the faith and sees their watchmen all blind, without spiritual knowledge [10], since they do not enjoy the gift of the Holy Spirit, the Giver of enlightenment; they have become like dogs unable to bark, unable to utter even a word for edification for the salvation of the flock, negligent and slack: “sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber” [10]. Their shepherds are like dogs that eat and do not bark, concerned with shameful gain, not with the benefit of the people, that is, greedy, who do not understand self-giving pastoral love [11]. They get drunk and make merry, and even invite others to share their drunkenness and luxury, reckoning that the life of revelry and luxury will last until tomorrow, and even expecting more luxury than they now have.

56.6.1.en: This is the picture of a pastoral care that lacks true divine love.

56.6.2.en: Whereas at the beginning of this chapter the Lord opens His spiritual house to all peoples without distinction, calling strangers to enjoy drawing near to Him and uniting with Him to receive fellowship in His eternal glories, and seeks even the fallen to return to Him that they may enjoy His love, He here contrasts that with the selfishness of some shepherds who have curled up around the “ego,” closing the doors of God’s mercies in the faces of people, seeking what is for their temporary pleasure at the expense of the salvation of others.
